approach: Add a Claude background-session backend to the CLI: with no multiplexer detected and harness claude, unit spawn hosts the unit in a Claude Code background session; a detected tmux/herdr still wins; cursor/codex still refuse. Selection is a spawn-level step keyed on harness; selectSessionAdapter and mux mode stay multiplexer-only.

Touches mux (selection), unit/registry (a new pane-locator kind), unit/lifecycle (spawn/close/nudge/read/focus/prune on the new backend). Expected to narrow one frozen mux scenario: the harness-agnostic no-multiplexer refusal becomes a refusal for harnesses with no background mode.
Clearance: in-session, the owner was shown that this narrows the frozen no-multiplexer refusal in mux and replied ok; the owner also chose automatic fallback over an opt-in flag.
Ringing a busy background unit (a Stop hook surfacing mail at end of turn) is held out of scope by the owner and tracked as issue 190; this CR reports such a send as not rung because busy.
leash auto-none: the owner is in-session; emit a verdict and stop at each gate rather than self-assert.
New ADR-0036 records the backend, the locator shape, and the stop-then-resume doorbell; ADR-0034 and ADR-0035 stay Proposed RFCs, out of scope.

why: Cold sdd-spec-judge round 4: oracle/builder/architect all PASS, ALIGNED true, no failing scenarios. New node unit/background specifies every per-unit operation on a unit hosted in a Claude background session; mux narrows its frozen no-multiplexer refusal to non-claude harnesses under the Clearance granted at seq 1 and adds three scenarios; unit/registry and mail/doorbell change additively. Four rounds: R1 pre-flight miss, R2 cross-node contract conflicts and uncovered failure edges, R3 an undefined active-record-with-stopped-session state introduced by R2's fixes, ruled invalid and out of contract by the owner in-session, R4 pass. Ratified by the owner in-session.

Re-open of two frozen suites during deliver, approved by the owner in-session. A live end-to-end run against real Claude Code disproved the ring's idleness signal (task state) in favour of the listing's turn status; two other frozen inputs were unconstructible (close Givens naming a leased worktree that lifecycle never refuses; a CLI flag that does not exist). Cold re-open judge: oracle/builder/architect PASS, ALIGNED true; the status repair fails the pre-repair implementation, the other two are input corrections with intent unchanged. Two advisory tightenings and one owner-requested additive scenario (closing a leased background unit) applied before re-freezing. Ratified by the owner in-session.
